subproblem.title: Local C¹ retraction onto an embedded C² submanifold with Lipschitz constants tending to 1
subproblem.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, N ⊆ ℝ^P an embedded C² d-dimensional submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N: every y ∈ N has an open W ∋ y and a map ψ, C² and injective on an open V ⊆ ℝ^d, with ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ injective on V), and x ∈ N. Then there are δ > 0 and π : ℝ^P → ℝ^P such that (i) π is C¹ on B_δ(x) = ball x δ; (ii) π maps B_δ(x) into N; (iii) π(y) = y for every y ∈ N ∩ B_δ(x); (iv) for every η > 0 there is s with 0 < s ≤ δ and |π(y) − π(z)| ≤ (1 + η)|y − z| for all y, z ∈ B_s(x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (N : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P), IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N → x ∈ N → ∃ (δ : ℝ) (π : Euclid P → Euclid P), 0 < δ ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 π (ball x δ) ∧ MapsTo π (ball x δ) N ∧ (∀ y ∈ N ∩ ball x δ, π y = y) ∧ ∀ η : ℝ, 0 < η → ∃ s : ℝ, 0 < s ∧ s ≤ δ ∧ ∀ y ∈ ball x s, ∀ z ∈ ball x s, ‖π y - π z‖ ≤ (1 + η) * ‖y - z‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Part III (RET) of the selected node's supplied proof. It replaces the nearest-point projection onto N used for the compactness theorem with constraint (Simon 7.2.5(2), chapter-07.txt lines 166–174) by an explicit graph retraction, which agrees with the nearest-point projection to first order at x; embedded submanifolds are as in Simon Ch. 2, §4 (4.1) (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold). No dependencies. Mathlib tools: the inverse function theorem (ContDiffAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph, ContDiffAt.localInverse, ContDiffAt.to_localInverse, OpenPartialHomeomorph.contDiffAt_symm), orthogonal projections (Submodule.starProjection, Submodule.starProjection_norm_le), LinearEquiv.ofInjective, and the mean value inequality (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le).
Notation: B_s(y) := ball y s ⊆ ℝ^P = Euclid P; B^d_s(0) := ball 0 s ⊆ ℝ^d = Euclid d; Df(v) := fderiv ℝ f v; ‖·‖ the operator norm.
1. (Chart at x.) Since x ∈ N, IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N gives an open V ⊆ ℝ^d, an open W ⊆ ℝ^P with x ∈ W, and ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P which is C² on V and injective on V, with ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(v) injective for every v ∈ V. As x ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V), choose v₀ ∈ V with ψ(v₀) = x. Since V is open and ψ is C² on V, ψ is differentiable at every point of V and Dψ is continuous on V. Put L := Dψ(v₀) : ℝ^d → ℝ^P, an injective continuous linear map; Q := L(ℝ^d), a (closed, finite-dimensional) subspace; L₀ : ℝ^d ≅ Q the linear isomorphism induced by L (LinearEquiv.ofInjective), continuous in finite dimension. Let p : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be the orthogonal projection onto Q (Q.starProjection): p is continuous linear, ‖p‖ ≤ 1, and p(q) = q for q ∈ Q. Define A := L₀⁻¹∘p : ℝ^P → ℝ^d (continuous linear; p regarded with values in Q). Then A(Lw) = L₀⁻¹(Lw) = w for w ∈ ℝ^d, i.e. A∘L = id, and L∘A = p.
2. (Local inverse.) Define h : ℝ^d → ℝ^d, h(v) := A(ψ(v) − x). Then h is C² on V (ψ followed by an affine map), h(v₀) = A(0) = 0, and Dh(v₀) = A∘Dψ(v₀) = A∘L = id. By the inverse function theorem there is an open set V₀ with v₀ ∈ V₀ ⊆ V such that O := h(V₀) is open, h maps V₀ bijectively onto O, and the inverse k : O → V₀ is C¹ on O with Dk(h(v)) = Dh(v)⁻¹ (shrinking V₀ we may assume Dh(v) is invertible for every v ∈ V₀, invertibility being an open condition and Dh continuous; then OpenPartialHomeomorph.contDiffAt_symm shows that k is C¹ at every point of O). Thus k(h(v)) = v for v ∈ V₀, k(u) ∈ V₀ and h(k(u)) = u for u ∈ O, 0 = h(v₀) ∈ O, k(0) = v₀ and Dk(0) = Dh(v₀)⁻¹ = id.
3. (Graph parametrization.) Φ := ψ∘k : O → ℝ^P is C¹ on O (k is C¹ on O with values in V₀ ⊆ V, where ψ is C²); Φ(0) = ψ(v₀) = x; Φ(O) = ψ(k(O)) = ψ(V₀) ⊆ ψ(V) ⊆ N; and DΦ(0) = Dψ(v₀)∘Dk(0) = L∘id = L.
4. (ψ(V₀) is relatively open in N.) Let F := V ∖ V₀. Claim: if y ∈ W and y = lim_i ψ(f_i) with all f_i ∈ F, then y ∈ ψ(F). Indeed K := {y} ∪ {ψ(f_i) : i ∈ ℕ} is compact (a convergent sequence together with its limit) and K ⊆ W (ψ(f_i) ∈ ψ(V) ⊆ W), so all f_i lie in the compact set V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K), and a subsequence f_{i_l} converges to some f ∈ V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K). As f_{i_l} ∉ V₀ and V₀ is open, f ∉ V₀, so f ∈ F; ψ is continuous at f ∈ V (V open), so ψ(f) = lim ψ(f_{i_l}) = y. Hence W ∩ closure(ψ(F)) = ψ(F) (recall ψ(F) ⊆ W), and W₀ := W ∖ ψ(F) = W ∩ (ℝ^P ∖ closure ψ(F)) is open. x ∈ W₀: x ∈ W, and if x = ψ(f) with f ∈ F ⊆ V then f = v₀ by injectivity of ψ on V, contradicting v₀ ∈ V₀. Finally W₀ ∩ N = ψ(V₀): if y ∈ W₀ ∩ N ⊆ W ∩ N = ψ(V), then y = ψ(v) with v ∈ V and v ∉ F (otherwise y ∈ ψ(F)), so v ∈ V₀; conversely ψ(V₀) ⊆ ψ(V) = W ∩ N, and ψ(V₀) ∩ ψ(F) = ∅ by injectivity of ψ on V (V₀ ∩ F = ∅).
5. (Choice of δ and π.) O is open and 0 ∈ O: choose r₀ > 0 with B^d_{r₀}(0) ⊆ O. W₀ is open and x ∈ W₀: choose δ > 0 with B_δ(x) ⊆ W₀ and ‖A‖·δ < r₀ (e.g. also δ < r₀/(‖A‖ + 1)). Define π : ℝ^P → ℝ^P by π(y) := Φ(A(y − x)) for y ∈ B_δ(x) and π(y) := y otherwise. For y ∈ B_δ(x), |A(y − x)| ≤ ‖A‖·|y − x| ≤ ‖A‖·δ < r₀, so A(y − x) ∈ B^d_{r₀}(0) ⊆ O.
6. ((i)–(iii).) (i) On the open ball B_δ(x), π coincides with Φ∘a, where a(y) := A(y − x) is affine (C^∞) and maps B_δ(x) into O, on which Φ is C¹; hence π is C¹ on B_δ(x) (ContDiffOn.comp, ContDiffOn.congr). (ii) For y ∈ B_δ(x), π(y) = Φ(A(y − x)) ∈ Φ(O) ⊆ N, so π maps B_δ(x) into N. (iii) If y ∈ N ∩ B_δ(x), then y ∈ N ∩ W₀ = ψ(V₀) by step 4, so y = ψ(v) with v ∈ V₀; then A(y − x) = h(v) ∈ O and π(y) = ψ(k(h(v))) = ψ(v) = y. In particular π(x) = x.
7. ((iv).) π is C¹ on the open set B_δ(x), so π is differentiable at every y ∈ B_δ(x) and Dπ is continuous on B_δ(x) (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen). By the chain rule (π = Φ∘a on a neighbourhood of y), Dπ(y) = DΦ(A(y − x))∘A for y ∈ B_δ(x); hence Dπ(x) = DΦ(0)∘A = L∘A = p and ‖Dπ(x)‖ ≤ 1. Let η > 0. By continuity of Dπ at x there is s with 0 < s ≤ δ and ‖Dπ(y) − Dπ(x)‖ ≤ η for all y ∈ B_s(x); then ‖Dπ(y)‖ ≤ ‖Dπ(x)‖ + η ≤ 1 + η on B_s(x). The ball B_s(x) is convex and π is differentiable on it, so the mean value inequality gives |π(y) − π(z)| ≤ (1 + η)|y − z| for all y, z ∈ B_s(x).
8. (Conclusion.) δ > 0 and π satisfy: π is C¹ on B_δ(x) (step 6(i)); π maps B_δ(x) into N (step 6(ii)); π(y) = y for y ∈ N ∩ B_δ(x) (step 6(iii)); and for every η > 0 there is s ∈ (0, δ] such that |π(y) − π(z)| ≤ (1 + η)|y − z| for all y, z ∈ B_s(x) (step 7). The case d = 0 is included: ℝ⁰ is a point, L = 0 is injective, Q = {0}, p = 0, A = 0, Φ ≡ x, π ≡ x on B_δ(x), and N ∩ B_δ(x) ⊆ ψ(V₀) = {x} by step 4. ∎
Note: this Lean type is byte-identical to that of the not yet accepted DAG node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.blowup_compactness-a1.local_retraction-a1 (dtc_bc_local_retraction), which follows the same plan (its children dtc_bc_lr_left_inverse_projection, dtc_bc_lr_local_inverse, dtc_bc_lr_chart_image_nhds and dtc_bc_lr_lipschitz_near_point correspond to steps 1, 2, 4 and 7); a later split of this node may reuse comparator-accepted declarations of that branch only when their frozen types are identical.
proof_key_steps: Take a chart ψ at x with ψ(v₀) = x, L := Dψ(v₀) injective, p the orthogonal projection onto Q = range L, and A := L⁻¹∘p (A∘L = id, L∘A = p).
The inverse function theorem for h := A(ψ − x) at v₀ gives V₀ ∋ v₀, O = h(V₀) ∋ 0 and a C¹ inverse k; Φ := ψ∘k parametrizes ψ(V₀) ⊆ N with DΦ(0) = L.
Properness of the chart makes ψ(V₀) relatively open in N: N ∩ W₀ = ψ(V₀) for an open W₀ ∋ x.
π(y) := Φ(A(y − x)) on a small B_δ(x) is C¹, maps into N, fixes N ∩ B_δ(x), and Dπ(x) = p has norm ≤ 1; continuity of Dπ and the mean value inequality give (1 + η)-Lipschitz bounds on small balls.

subproblem.title: Rescaled retractions onto the blown-up constraint sets η_{x_j,λ_j}(U ∩ N) at moving centres
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, N ⊆ ℝ^P with (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, and x ∈ U. Assume that if x ∈ N there are δ > 0 and π : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with π C¹ on B_δ(x), π(B_δ(x)) ⊆ N, π(y) = y for y ∈ N ∩ B_δ(x), and for every η > 0 some s ∈ (0, δ] with |π(y) − π(z)| ≤ (1 + η)|y − z| for y, z ∈ B_s(x). Let x_j ∈ ℝ^P with x_j → x and λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0, and A_j := η_{x_j,λ_j}(U ∩ N) (η_{x_j,λ_j} = dilation x_j λ_j). Then for every G > 0 there are maps π_j : ℝ^P → ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ) and G′ ∈ ℝ such that: for all large j, either A_j ∩ B_G(0) = ∅, or π_j is C¹ on B_G(0), maps B_G(0) into A_j ∩ B_{G′}(0) and π_j(y) = y for y ∈ A_j ∩ B_G(0); and for every η > 0, for all large j, either A_j ∩ B_G(0) = ∅ or |π_j(y) − π_j(z)| ≤ (1 + η)|y − z| for all y, z ∈ B_G(0). (B_s(y) = ball y s; 'for all large j' = eventually in atTop.)

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Part II.5–6 of the selected node's supplied proof (retractions onto N as in Simon 7.2.5(2), chapter-07.txt lines 166–174, rescaled for the blow-ups in the proof of 7.3.1, lines 317–337; the subsequence Cases A/B of the grandparent's proof become the disjunctions in the conclusion). No dependencies: the local retraction at x is a hypothesis, namely the conclusion of the sibling local_retraction, which the selected parent applies to N at x with d := m + 1 + ℓ when x ∈ N.
Notation: λ_j := lams j > 0, x_j := xs j, η_j := dilation x_j λ_j, so η_j(y) = −λ_j⁻¹x_j + λ_j⁻¹y = λ_j⁻¹(y − x_j); A_j := η_j(U ∩ N); B_s(y) := ball y s; a_j(z) := x_j + λ_jz. 'For all large j' means eventually in atTop. Fix G > 0.
1. (Elementary facts.) (a) η_j(a_j(z)) = λ_j⁻¹(λ_jz) = z for every z, and for every S ⊆ ℝ^P, z ∈ η_j(S) iff a_j(z) ∈ S (if z = η_j(y) then y = x_j + λ_jλ_j⁻¹(y − x_j) = a_j(z)). (b) If z ∈ B_G(0) and |x_j − x| + λ_jG ≤ t, then a_j(z) ∈ B_t(x), because |a_j(z) − x| ≤ |x_j − x| + λ_j|z| < |x_j − x| + λ_jG ≤ t. (c) For every c ∈ ℝ and t > 0, |x_j − x| + λ_jc → 0 (x_j → x, λ_j → 0), so |x_j − x| + λ_jc < t for all large j.
2. (Case A: x ∉ N.) Then x ∉ closure N, since otherwise x ∈ (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅ (x ∈ U). As closure N is closed, there is r_N > 0 with B_{r_N}(x) ∩ closure N = ∅. Put π_j := id for every j and G′ := 0. By 1(c) (c := G, t := r_N), |x_j − x| + λ_jG < r_N for all large j, and for such j, A_j ∩ B_G(0) = ∅: if z ∈ A_j ∩ B_G(0), then u := a_j(z) ∈ U ∩ N by 1(a) and u ∈ B_{r_N}(x) by 1(b), contradicting B_{r_N}(x) ∩ N = ∅. Hence the first eventual statement holds through its first alternative, and so does the second, for every η > 0 (same eventual set of j).
3. (Case B: x ∈ N, set-up.) The hypothesis gives δ > 0 and π : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with (i) π C¹ on B_δ(x), (ii) π(B_δ(x)) ⊆ N, (iii) π(y) = y for y ∈ N ∩ B_δ(x), (iv) for every η > 0 some s(η) ∈ (0, δ] with |π(y) − π(z)| ≤ (1 + η)|y − z| for y, z ∈ B_{s(η)}(x). Let s₁ := s(1) ∈ (0, δ], so π is 2-Lipschitz on B_{s₁}(x). U is open and x ∈ U: choose r > 0 with B_r(x) ⊆ U. Define, for every j, π_j(z) := η_j(π(a_j(z))) = λ_j⁻¹(π(x_j + λ_jz) − x_j), and G′ := 5G.
4. (Case B, first statement.) By 1(c), for all large j both |x_j − x| + λ_jG < s₁ and |x_j − x| + 5λ_jG < r hold. Fix such j. By 1(b), a_j maps B_G(0) into B_{s₁}(x) ⊆ B_δ(x). If A_j ∩ B_G(0) = ∅, the first alternative holds. Otherwise fix z₀ ∈ A_j ∩ B_G(0); we prove the second alternative. (a) (C¹.) a_j is affine (C^∞) and maps B_G(0) into B_δ(x), where π is C¹; η_j is a constant plus the continuous linear map λ_j⁻¹·id, hence C^∞; so π_j = η_j∘π∘a_j is C¹ on B_G(0) (ContDiffOn.comp, ContDiff.comp_contDiffOn). (b) (Identity.) Let z ∈ A_j ∩ B_G(0). By 1(a), u := a_j(z) ∈ U ∩ N, and u ∈ B_δ(x) by 1(b); by (iii), π(u) = u, so π_j(z) = η_j(u) = η_j(a_j(z)) = z. (c) (Range.) w := a_j(z₀) ∈ U ∩ N by 1(a), and w ∈ B_{s₁}(x) by 1(b), so π(w) = w by (iii). Let z ∈ B_G(0) and y := a_j(z) ∈ B_{s₁}(x). Then π(y) ∈ N by (ii), and, as |z − z₀| ≤ |z| + |z₀| < 2G, |π(y) − x_j| ≤ |π(y) − π(w)| + |w − x_j| ≤ 2|y − w| + λ_j|z₀| = 2λ_j|z − z₀| + λ_j|z₀| < 4λ_jG + λ_jG = 5λ_jG. Hence |π(y) − x| ≤ |π(y) − x_j| + |x_j − x| < 5λ_jG + |x_j − x| < r, so π(y) ∈ B_r(x) ⊆ U and π(y) ∈ U ∩ N. Therefore π_j(z) = η_j(π(y)) ∈ A_j and |π_j(z)| = λ_j⁻¹|π(y) − x_j| < 5G = G′, i.e. π_j(z) ∈ A_j ∩ B_{G′}(0). Thus, for all large j, A_j ∩ B_G(0) = ∅, or π_j is C¹ on B_G(0), maps B_G(0) into A_j ∩ B_{G′}(0) and is the identity on A_j ∩ B_G(0).
5. (Case B, second statement.) Let η > 0 and s := s(η). By 1(c), |x_j − x| + λ_jG < s for all large j; fix such j and y, z ∈ B_G(0). By 1(b), a_j(y), a_j(z) ∈ B_s(x), and |a_j(y) − a_j(z)| = λ_j|y − z|. So the second alternative holds for all large j.
6. (Conclusion.) In both cases the maps π_j and the radius G′ are chosen before η, and steps 2, 4 and 5 give the two eventual statements, for every G > 0. ∎

subproblem.title: Locally bounded masses of blow-ups at moving centres, from the monotonicity inequality
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) an integer multiplicity current (IsIntegerMultiplicity T). Assume: for every compact K ⊆ U there is Λ ≥ 0 such that for all y ∈ ℝ^P and R ∈ ℝ with closedBall(y, R) ⊆ K the function ρ ↦ ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ)·M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) (values in [0, ∞]) is monotone on (0, R). Let x ∈ U, x_j ∈ ℝ^P with x_j → x, and λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0. Then for every R ∈ ℝ there is c ∈ [0, ∞) (c ≠ ∞) such that M_{B_R(0)}(blowUp T x_j λ_j) ≤ c for all large j (eventually in atTop), where B_R(0) = ball 0 R and blowUp T x_j λ_j = η_{x_j,λ_j#}T ∈ 𝒟_n(η_{x_j,λ_j}(U)).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Part II.4 of the selected node's supplied proof (Simon 7.3.1, proof, chapter-07.txt lines 325–331: the scaling identity (ωₙRⁿ)⁻¹M_{B_R(0)}(η_{x,λ_j#}T) = (ωₙλ_jⁿRⁿ)⁻¹M_{B_{λ_jR}(x)}(T) together with the monotonicity formula gives sup_j M_{B_R(0)}(η_{x,λ_j#}T) < ∞; here the centres x_j move). Dependencies (siblings): mass_and_support = Submission.dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support (MR: for U open and an IMRep R₀ representing T, M_W(T) = R₀.measure(W) for every open W) and blowup_mass_scaling = Submission.dtc_blowUp_massOn_image (MS: for λ > 0 and every W, M_{η_{a,λ}(W)}(blowUp T a λ) = ofReal((λ⁻¹)ⁿ)·M_W(T)).
Notation: λ_j := lams j > 0, x_j := xs j, η_j := dilation x_j λ_j (η_j(y) = λ_j⁻¹(y − x_j)), S_j := blowUp T x_j λ_j, B_s(y) := ball y s; 'for all large j' means eventually in atTop.
1. (Radius.) U is open and x ∈ U, so there is ε > 0 with B_ε(x) ⊆ U; put r := ε/3 > 0. Then K := closedBall(x, 2r) ⊆ B_ε(x) ⊆ U, and K is compact (closed balls of ℝ^P are compact).
2. (Monotonicity.) The hypothesis applied to K gives Λ ≥ 0 such that for all y ∈ ℝ^P and s ∈ ℝ with closedBall(y, s) ⊆ K, the function f_y(ρ) := ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ)·M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) ∈ [0, ∞] is monotone (nondecreasing) on (0, s).
3. (Finite mass near x.) T is integer multiplicity; let R₀ = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep representing T in U. By MR (U and B_{2r}(x) open), M_{B_{2r}(x)}(T) = R₀.measure(B_{2r}(x)) ≤ R₀.measure(K) (B_{2r}(x) ⊆ K). By definition R₀.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ, so, K being Borel, R₀.measure(K) = ∫_K θ d(Hⁿ⌞M) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict), which is finite by the local integrability of θ (R₀.locallyIntegrable_mult, K compact ⊆ U). Hence M_{B_{2r}(x)}(T) < ∞ and c₁ := ofReal(e^{Λr}(2/r)ⁿ)·M_{B_{2r}(x)}(T) is finite.
4. (Uniform density bound near x.) Claim: if |y − x| < r and 0 < ρ < r/2, then M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) ≤ ofReal(ρⁿ)·c₁. (a) closedBall(y, r) ⊆ K, since |z − y| ≤ r gives |z − x| ≤ |z − y| + |y − x| < 2r. By step 2 with s := r, f_y is monotone on (0, r); as ρ and r/2 lie in (0, r) and ρ ≤ r/2, f_y(ρ) ≤ f_y(r/2) = ofReal(e^{Λr/2}/(r/2)ⁿ)·M_{B_{r/2}(y)}(T). (b) B_{r/2}(y) ⊆ B_{2r}(x) (|z − x| < r/2 + r), so M_{B_{r/2}(y)}(T) ≤ M_{B_{2r}(x)}(T) (massOn is monotone in the set, GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono); and e^{Λr/2}/(r/2)ⁿ = e^{Λr/2}(2/r)ⁿ ≤ e^{Λr}(2/r)ⁿ since Λ ≥ 0 and r > 0. Hence f_y(r/2) ≤ c₁. (c) Since Λρ ≥ 0, e^{Λρ} ≥ 1, so ρ^{−n} ≤ e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ and ofReal(ρ^{−n})·M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) ≤ f_y(ρ) ≤ c₁. Multiplying by ofReal(ρⁿ) and using ofReal(ρⁿ)·ofReal(ρ^{−n}) = ofReal(1) = 1 (ρ > 0) gives M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) ≤ ofReal(ρⁿ)·c₁.
